lines.text: I thought Projects was Cowork for non-technical people. I was wrong. It is much more powerful.
Since then I used it to build my whole Clawd harness: skills, rules and hooks, all inside one project, a team OS.
I gave the main chat one goal. It split the work into threads and ran them in parallel.

Here is what I missed. Every thread is a full session, on its own branch, in the cloud. Close the laptop and a cloud thread keeps going, and you can check in from your phone. Need your local files? Ask, and it runs on your machine.
A thread opens its own pull request, then watches it. When CI fails, it pushes the fix, and it answers review comments. I raised several PRs this way without leaving the project.
The library holds the files you add and the files threads produce. And a daily routine can open a new thread when it finds a regression.
Now, three tips from the Clawd Code team for managing the coordinator.
One. Every thread uses your plan's limits. Leave the coordinator on low effort, and use a smaller model for the threads.
Two. Tell it how many threads to run, how often to update you, and to show a plan first.
Three. Threads share memory. Teach it a preference once, and every thread knows.
Projects is in beta for Pro and Max, not Team or Enterprise yet. No clear verdict yet, but I will be using it more often.

notes: Spoken text spells Claude as 'Clawd'. On-screen text keeps 'Claude'.
